reference_sql:
WITH first_days AS (  -- one row per customer
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(CAST(order_ts AS DATE)) AS first_day
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS returning_customers
FROM first_days f
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.customer_id = f.customer_id
    AND CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) > f.first_day
    AND CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) <= f.first_day + INTERVAL 30 DAY
)

WITH first_days AS (  -- one row per customer
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(CAST(order_ts AS DATE)) AS first_day
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT f.customer_id) AS returning_customers
FROM first_days f

 AND CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) > f.first_day
 AND CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) <= f.first_day + 30

other_way.tradeoff: A join with COUNT(DISTINCT ...) gives the same count, but EXISTS stops at the first match and can never count a customer twice.

solver.query:
WITH first_day AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(CAST(order_ts AS DATE)) AS d0
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT f.customer_id) AS returning_customers
FROM first_day f
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = f.customer_id
WHERE CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) > f.d0
  AND CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) <= f.d0 + 30
